# Third-party attributions

<!-- Generated from `sidecars.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` by `cargo xtask check-notices --update`. Do not edit by hand: `cargo xtask check-notices` fails when this file and those inputs disagree. -->

Peregrine itself is dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 (see `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE`). This is the attribution inventory a redistribution of Peregrine must carry. It exists for users and distributors, and it is derived rather than hand-written so it cannot drift from the lockfiles.

## Bundled sidecar executables

These are separate programs invoked as subprocesses and never linked into the application binary, so they are aggregated with Peregrine rather than derived from it (`docs/adr/0009-licensing-and-redistribution.md`). Each ships with its licence text, the build configuration below, and a written offer of corresponding source on the same distribution channel as the binary.

### mpv

- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-or-later
- **Version pin:** pinned per OS; the exact version and SHA-256 for each platform are recorded by the release bundling work (`docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §1)
- **Upstream source:** https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv
- **Written offer of corresponding source:** Written offer: the complete corresponding source for the exact binary shipped, with the recorded build configuration and any patch we carry, is published on the same distribution channel as the binary at https://github.com/peregrine-app/peregrine/releases
- **Why it is a separate executable:** GPL copyleft, so linking it would put that code inside our binary (docs/adr/0009). An LGPL-only build is not an escape: it disables Linux X11 video output (docs/adr/0013). The official macOS and Windows builds are GPL-3.0 as shipped because they embed FFmpeg built with --enable-gpl --enable-version3.
- **Build configuration:** macOS and Windows: the official upstream release build, unpatched, pinned by asset and SHA-256 in packaging/sidecars.lock.json. Linux: built in CI from mpv-build at the pinned commit in a digest-pinned Ubuntu image. The source offer names the mpv commit, the FFmpeg source embedded in the official builds, and the meson configuration (docs/adr/0025).

### ffmpeg

- **Licence:** LGPL-3.0-or-later
- **Version pin:** pinned per OS; the exact version and SHA-256 for each platform are recorded by the release bundling work (`docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §1)
- **Upstream source:** https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg
- **Written offer of corresponding source:** Written offer: the complete corresponding source for the exact binary shipped, with the recorded `configure` line and any patch we carry, is published on the same distribution channel as the binary at https://github.com/peregrine-app/peregrine/releases
- **Why it is a separate executable:** LGPL, so linking libav* would put copyleft code inside our binary (docs/adr/0009). Running it as a subprocess also gives crash isolation for codecs we do not control.
- **Build configuration:** LGPL-only: no `--enable-gpl` and no `--enable-nonfree`. `--enable-version3` is accepted, so the licence is LGPL-3.0-or-later on every platform (docs/adr/0025). Windows and Linux are pinned BtbN LGPL builds; macOS is built in CI. The exact `configure` line and any `git diff` ship beside the pinned version. Distributed as an on-demand component pack, not in the base install.

### ffprobe

- **Licence:** LGPL-3.0-or-later
- **Version pin:** pinned per OS; the exact version and SHA-256 for each platform are recorded by the release bundling work (`docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §1)
- **Upstream source:** https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg
- **Written offer of corresponding source:** Written offer: the complete corresponding source for the exact binary shipped, with the recorded `configure` line and any patch we carry, is published on the same distribution channel as the binary at https://github.com/peregrine-app/peregrine/releases
- **Why it is a separate executable:** Same build and licence as `ffmpeg`; no in-process probe reports HDR mastering or dynamic metadata (docs/DEPENDENCIES.md §5), and LGPL code stays outside the process boundary (docs/adr/0009).
- **Build configuration:** The ffprobe binary of the same ffmpeg build declared above, so one `configure` line covers both. Ships in the base install.

### prowlarr

- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-or-later
- **Version pin:** pinned per OS; the exact version and SHA-256 for each platform are recorded by the release bundling work (`docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §1)
- **Upstream source:** https://github.com/Prowlarr/Prowlarr
- **Written offer of corresponding source:** Written offer: the complete corresponding source for the exact binary, as published by the Prowlarr project, is at https://github.com/Prowlarr/Prowlarr/releases/tag/v2.6.5.5623; we ship the upstream release artefact unpatched, and the same pinned artefact is republished on our distribution channel with this offer.
- **Why it is a separate executable:** GPL-3.0-or-later, so it runs out of process as a managed sidecar (docs/adr/0009, R25). It is an indexer manager, not part of the media path.
- **Build configuration:** Upstream release build, unpatched. Installed on demand as a component pack (docs/adr/0024): osx-app-core-arm64.zip on macOS, linux-core-x64.tar.gz on Linux, windows-core-x64.zip on Windows, each pinned by size and SHA-256 per docs/DEPENDENCIES.md §1.

### 7zz

- **Licence:** LGPL-2.1-or-later
- **Version pin:** pinned per OS; the exact version and SHA-256 for each platform are recorded by the release bundling work (`docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §1)
- **Upstream source:** https://github.com/ip7z/7zip
- **Written offer of corresponding source:** Written offer: the complete corresponding source for the exact 7-Zip release we ship is published by the 7-Zip project at https://www.7-zip.org/download.html; the upstream archive is republished unpatched beside our binary.
- **Why it is a separate executable:** LGPL-2.1-or-later with 7-Zip's unRAR restriction, so it runs as a separate executable (docs/adr/0009). It is the archive reader for a Usenet RAR/7z set (docs/adr/0030).
- **Build configuration:** Upstream release build, unpatched, pinned by asset and SHA-256 in the release manifest. The macOS and Linux archives carry the 7zz binary; Windows uses the console build from the upstream extra package.

### par2

- **Licence:** GPL-2.0-or-later
- **Version pin:** pinned per OS; the exact version and SHA-256 for each platform are recorded by the release bundling work (`docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §1)
- **Upstream source:** https://github.com/Parchive/par2cmdline
- **Written offer of corresponding source:** Written offer: the complete corresponding source for the exact par2cmdline release is published at https://github.com/Parchive/par2cmdline/releases/tag/v1.4.0; the upstream binary is republished unpatched beside our binary.
- **Why it is a separate executable:** GPL-2.0-or-later, so it runs as a separate executable (docs/adr/0009). It verifies and repairs a Usenet par2 set (docs/adr/0030).
- **Build configuration:** Upstream release binary, unpatched, pinned by asset and SHA-256 in the release manifest for each supported platform.

## Rust dependencies

The application binary (`peregrine-desktop`) resolves to the 707 crates below: the non-development dependency closure read from `Cargo.lock`, so test runners, mocks, and benchmark harnesses are excluded. Cargo does not record dependency kinds in `Cargo.lock`, so a crate that only a third-party build script uses can remain in the list; over-attributing is safe, and every crate linked at runtime is present.

Licence expressions and texts are not repeated here: `cargo deny check` enforces them against the allowlist in `deny.toml`, and the release's bundled-licence manifest and SBOM must carry the texts. The special obligations in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §6 apply to this list.

## Frontend packages

The compiled frontend (`apps/desktop/dist`) bundles the 82 packages below. They are the runtime closure of `apps/desktop` and of the workspace packages it links, read from `pnpm-lock.yaml` by following `dependencies` and `optionalDependencies`.

Development-only packages are not redistributed and cannot appear here: pnpm records a workspace project's development dependencies in the lockfile but never resolves their transitive dependencies, so the Vite, ESLint, and Vitest toolchains have no edge into this walk. An optional *peer* that pnpm auto-installed for another package's types (`typescript`, `@types/react`) is excluded for the same reason: the bundle imports no code from it.

Licence expressions and texts are not repeated here: `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §3 records the reviewed licence and purpose of each package, and the release's `pnpm licenses list --json` manifest carries the texts. `pnpm check-dead-deps` fails on a declared dependency nothing imports, so no package is listed merely because a manifest mentions it.
